notes.evidence: (b) Height. Except as provided in paragraph (h) of this part, the nationality and registration marks must be of equal height and on— (1) Fixed-wing aircraft, must be at least 12 inches high,

notes.front: How wide must registration characters be, and which character is the exception at one-sixth?
notes.back: Two-thirds as wide as high; the number 1 is one-sixth as wide as high.
notes.explanation: The letters M and W may be as wide as they are high.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 45 (1 January 2025 edition), § 45.29(c)
notes.evidence: (c) Width. Characters must be twothirds as wide as they are high, except the number ‘‘1’’, which must be onesixth as wide as it is high, and the let- ters ‘‘M’’ and ‘‘W’’ which may be as wide as they are high.

notes.front: How thick must the lines forming registration characters be?
notes.back: Solid lines one-sixth as thick as the character is high.
notes.explanation: The lines must also be solid.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 45 (1 January 2025 edition), § 45.29(d)
notes.evidence: (d) Thickness. Characters must be formed by solid lines one-sixth as thick as the character is high.

notes.front: A mechanic lays out 12-inch registration marks on an aeroplane’s fuselage. How wide is each ordinary character, and how thick is each line?
notes.back: D: 8 inches wide, 2-inch lines.
notes.choices:
A) 12 in wide, 3 in thick
B) 6 in wide, 1 in thick
C) 8 in wide, 3 in thick
D) 8 in wide, 2 in thick
notes.choicesExplained: A uses full height for width and a quarter for thickness. B uses half and one-twelfth. C gets the width right but uses a quarter for thickness.
notes.explanation: Two-thirds of 12 is 8; one-sixth of 12 is 2.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 45 (1 January 2025 edition), § 45.29(c)–(d)
notes.evidence: (c) Width. Characters must be twothirds as wide as they are high, except the number ‘‘1’’, which must be onesixth as wide as it is high, and the let- ters ‘‘M’’ and ‘‘W’’ which may be as wide as they are high. (d) Thickness. Characters must be formed by solid lines one-sixth as thick as the character is high.

notes.front: Where must a fixed-wing aircraft display its registration marks?
notes.back: On the vertical tail surfaces or the sides of the fuselage.
notes.explanation: Either place satisfies the rule, subject to the exception in § 45.29(f).
notes.source: 14 CFR part 45 (1 January 2025 edition), § 45.25(a)
notes.evidence: (a) The operator of a fixed-wing aircraft must display the required marks on either the vertical tail surfaces or the sides of the fuselage, except as provided in § 45.29(f).

notes.front: Where must a manufacturer secure the data plate on an aircraft?
notes.back: On the fuselage exterior, legible from the ground, aft of the rear-most entrance door or near the tail surfaces.
notes.explanation: Paragraphs (d) to (h) allow other locations for some aircraft.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 45 (1 January 2025 edition), § 45.11(a)(3)
notes.evidence: (3) Except as provided in paragraphs (d) through (h) of this section, must be secured to the aircraft fuselage exterior so that it is legible to a person on the ground, and must be either adjacent to and aft of the rear-most entrance door or on the fuselage surface near the tail surfaces.

notes.front: Which rating must an aircraft engine’s identification data include under § 45.13?
notes.back: Its established rating.
notes.explanation: Type and production certificate numbers, by contrast, are required only if they exist.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 45 (1 January 2025 edition), § 45.13(a)
notes.evidence: (4) Type certificate number, if any. (5) Production certificate number, if any. (6) For aircraft engines, the established rating.

notes.front: Which three items identifying the maker and the product head the § 45.13 list of identification data?
notes.back: Builder’s name, model designation and builder’s serial number.
notes.explanation: The same data goes on aircraft, engines and propellers under § 45.11.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 45 (1 January 2025 edition), § 45.13(a)
notes.evidence: (a) The identification required by § 45.11 (a) through (c) must include the following information: (1) Builder’s name. (2) Model designation. (3) Builder’s serial number.

notes.front: During a repaint, a mechanic working under part 43 removes a data plate. What may they do with it?
notes.back: D: reinstall it only on the same aircraft.
notes.choices:
A) Fit it to any aircraft of the same model
B) Discard it and order a new one
C) Keep it as a spare
D) Reinstall it only on the aircraft it came from
notes.choicesExplained: A and C: a removed plate may go on no other aircraft. B is not what the rule provides.
notes.explanation: Part 43 lets the plate come off when maintenance needs it, but ties it to the product it came from.
notes.source: 14 CFR part 45 (1 January 2025 edition), § 45.13(d)–(e)
notes.evidence: (2) Remove an identification plate required by § 45.11 when necessary during maintenance operations. (e) No person may install an identification plate removed in accordance with paragraph (d)(2) of this section on any aircraft, aircraft engine, propeller, propeller blade, or propeller hub other than the one from which it was removed.
